sources.title: How Can We Help Kids With Transitions?
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute (Martinelli), last updated 15 Sep 2025
sources.quote: give a time frame and description of what will happen along with countdowns ... allows them to emotionally get ready for an event ... Being able to point to a chart with drawings about what to expect from a particular transition ... Other kids may benefit from visual cues.
sources.supports: Giving a time frame, a description of what will happen and countdowns helps a child get ready emotionally; drawings and visual cues help some children. The page is about transitions, applied here to waiting for a birthday.

sources.title: Create a Kid's Calendar in Two Ways
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents, 23 Jul 2018
sources.quote: Waiting for big events like birthdays, holidays, or the start of school are great opportunities
sources.supports: A big event such as a birthday is a chance for a child to learn to keep track of days and months on a calendar. The page does not describe a birthday countdown as such; the daily crossing off is our example.

sources.title: Helping Kids Learn to Take Turns and Practice Waiting
sources.publisher: PBS KIDS for Parents (Samantha Gratton), 4 Aug 2023
sources.quote: Waiting is hard (even for grown-ups)! ... You can also use a timer that shows a countdown for taking turns! ... gave each person something else to do while they waited! ... Talking about what comes next can comfort your child and remind them who gets the next turn.
sources.supports: Waiting is hard, a visual countdown timer helps, something else to do while waiting helps, and talking about what comes next comforts a child and says who has the next turn.

sources.title: How to help your preschooler manage overexcitement
sources.publisher: Understood, 5 Aug 2019
sources.quote: Prep your child ... Plan on giving a five-minute notice when you see they start to get louder and too excited.
sources.supports: Prepare the child ahead and give a five-minute notice when a preschooler gets louder and too excited. The page is about overexcitement in general, applied to the days before a birthday.
